fixes.explanation: That's the one. The LORD asks, "Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb?" (Isaiah 49:15). A mother forgetting her nursing child is hard to picture. Then He says that even if she could forget, He will not forget Zion.

I get why you'd pick it, but her name never comes up. The LORD asks, "Can a woman forget her nursing child, or lack compassion for the son of her womb?" (Isaiah 49:15). The question is about a child, not a name. Then He says He won't forget Zion even if she could.

Builders, yes, friend! The verse says, "Your builders hasten back; your destroyers and wreckers depart from you." (Isaiah 49:17). The ones who tear down are leaving. The ones who rebuild are in a hurry to get back. That's a big change for Zion in one verse.

Yes, they carry them to her. The Lord GOD says, "They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders." (Isaiah 49:22). He lifts His hand and raises His banner to the nations, and the sons are brought in arms while the daughters are carried on shoulders. That's a gentle way to travel, friend.

It's the opposite direction. The Lord GOD says, "They will bring your sons in their arms and carry your daughters on their shoulders." (Isaiah 49:22). The nations bring them toward Zion, not away from her. Arms for the sons, shoulders for the daughters.

Fathers, that's right. The LORD says, "Kings will be your foster fathers, and their queens your nursing mothers." (Isaiah 49:23). Kings are her foster fathers and queens are her nursing mothers. That's quite a household for Zion.
Masters sounds like a boss, friend, and that's not the word. Here the kings are called foster fathers (Isaiah 49:23). Their queens are called nursing mothers. Not a boss in sight.

That's the promise. The LORD says Zion will know that He is the LORD. Then comes the promise: "those who hope in Me will never be put to shame." (Isaiah 49:23). Hope placed in Him doesn't end in shame.

True. Verse 24 asks, "Can the plunder be snatched from the mighty, or the captives of a tyrant be delivered?" Then the LORD says, "Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved…" (Isaiah 49:25). That question sounds like a hard one. The answer given is yes, they will be taken away.

It's actually true, friend. Look at what the LORD says in verse 25: "Even the captives of the mighty will be taken away, and the plunder of the tyrant will be retrieved…" (Isaiah 49:25). Those are His words, so the statement on the card matches them. The captives are taken away from the mighty.

Not the builders, friend. In verse 17 they hasten back to her, and that's a different thing from what the LORD says here. He says, "I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children." (Isaiah 49:25). He contends with those who contend with Zion.

The nations show up in verse 22, bringing her sons. The Lord GOD says, "They will bring your sons in their arms…" (Isaiah 49:22). Then the LORD says, "I will contend with those who contend with you, and I will save your children." (Isaiah 49:25). So it's the ones who contend with her.
